nodes.label: Paper Trading Fee/Slippage Simulation Model
nodes.rationale: Paper execution simulates fills against live orderbook data with configurable slippage (bps against best bid/ask) and mirrors CoinDCX's real fee schedule: 0.5% trading fee on trade value both sides, +18% GST on that fee, plus 1% TDS (Income Tax Act s.194S) on trade value on sells only — so paper PnL stays directly comparable to real trading. Constants live in paper.py for adjustment if CoinDCX's schedule changes.

nodes.label: dashboard/AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated and re-added by `next dev` (see node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js) to warn that this Next.js version has breaking changes vs. training data — read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code and heed deprecation notices. Committing the block with other work keeps the tree clean since removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change.

nodes.label: Autonomous Bug Fixing
nodes.rationale: Given a bug report, just fix it — point at logs/errors/failing tests and resolve them with zero context-switching required from the user, including fixing failing CI tests without being told how.

nodes.label: Core Principles (Simplicity/No Laziness/Minimal Impact)
nodes.rationale: Simplicity first (make every change as simple as possible, minimal code impact); no laziness (find root causes, no temporary fixes, senior developer standards); minimal impact (changes only touch what's necessary, avoid introducing bugs).

nodes.label: Demand Elegance (Balanced)
nodes.rationale: For non-trivial changes, pause and ask if there's a more elegant way; if a fix feels hacky, implement the elegant solution knowing everything now known; skip this for simple, obvious fixes.

nodes.label: Plan Mode Default
nodes.rationale: Enter plan mode for any non-trivial task (3+ steps or architectural decisions); if something goes sideways, stop and re-plan immediately rather than keep pushing; write detailed specs upfront to reduce ambiguity.

nodes.label: Self-Improvement Loop
nodes.rationale: After any correction from the user, update tasks/lessons.md with the pattern and write rules that prevent the same mistake; ruthlessly iterate on these lessons until the mistake rate drops; review lessons at session start.

nodes.label: Subagent Strategy
nodes.rationale: Offload research, exploration, and parallel analysis to subagents to keep the main context window clean; throw more compute at complex problems via subagents; one task per subagent for focused execution.

nodes.label: Task Management process
nodes.rationale: Plan first (tasks/todo.md with checkable items), verify the plan before implementing, track progress as items complete, explain changes at each step, document results, and capture lessons after corrections.

nodes.label: Daily Max-Loss Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: Daily max-loss is a hard circuit breaker, not a guarantee: once realized loss hits max_daily_loss the bot stops opening new positions and flattens all open positions immediately; this only bounds realized loss to approximately the threshold plus flattening slippage since markets can gap and orders can fail. Stays blocked until the next IST trading day.

nodes.label: Free-Tier Deployment Topology
nodes.rationale: Free-tier-only: GitHub Actions cron for trading_cycle (*/10 min), risk_check (*/5 min, GH Actions' shortest interval), and evolution (nightly) workflows invoking the same orchestrator/evolution_agent scripts used locally; Supabase free-tier Postgres for storage; Vercel-hosted Next.js dashboard reading Supabase directly via a read-only anon key + RLS, no separate backend server. GitHub Actions cron is best-effort, not guaranteed — runs can be delayed under platform load, so daily bookkeeping recomputes from trades/daily_pnl rather than trusting cycle count.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Architecture (one cycle, run-to-completion)
nodes.rationale: All agents are separate, independently testable Python modules under src/agents/. One full cycle (data → signal → risk → execute → log) runs to completion and exits — no long-running process, since GH Actions free-tier cron re-invokes the script each interval instead of keeping a daemon alive.

nodes.label: Fixed % Position Sizing Rule
nodes.rationale: Fixed % of capital_to_use per trade (position_size_pct, default 10%), capped at max_concurrent_positions (default 5) simultaneous positions. At defaults, at most 50% of allocated capital is deployed at once — a deliberate buffer, not a hard requirement.

nodes.label: Real-Trading Promotion Criteria
nodes.rationale: Configurable via env vars rather than a DB table because these change rarely and don't need versioning: PROMOTION_MIN_PAPER_DAYS (default 14), PROMOTION_MIN_CUMULATIVE_PNL (default 0), PROMOTION_MAX_DRAWDOWN_PCT (default 15). Evolution Agent checks these against the current paper version and sets promoted_to_real when met.

nodes.label: promoted_to_real Gate
nodes.rationale: Real trading only ever runs a strategy_versions.promoted_to_real = true version. The gate lives in the orchestrator (not just the execution agent) so there is no path that reaches real order placement with an unpromoted strategy. RealExecutionAgent adds the same 1% sell-side TDS on top of the exchange-reported fee since TDS isn't a documented response field — unverified against a real fill because account balance was under CoinDCX's ₹100 min_notional at build time.

nodes.label: Verification Before Done
nodes.rationale: Never mark a task complete without proving it works: diff behavior between main and the change when relevant, run tests, check logs, demonstrate correctness — 'would a staff engineer approve this?'

nodes.label: LLM Provider Abstraction (Groq/Ollama fallback chain)
nodes.rationale: Provider is configurable (LLM_PROVIDER=groq default or ollama via Ollama Cloud); groq_client.py's chat() is the single entry point both Signal and Evolution agents call with the same retry/fallback/logging behavior either way, so switching providers is an env var change, not a code change. On 429/error: exponential backoff on the current model, then fallback to the next model in the configurable GROQ_MODEL_CHAIN/OLLAMA_MODEL_CHAIN, logging every attempt to model_usage. Verified during build by forcing a failure to confirm the fallback chain actually triggers, rather than trusting the retry logic unexercised.

nodes.label: Stop-Loss/Take-Profit Polling Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Per-trade stop_loss_pct/take_profit_pct from the active strategy version's params_json are enforced against live ticker price independent of the LLM signal. Not a guarantee: CoinDCX's spot API has no exchange-side stop order (stop-limit/take-profit exist only in the margin product, deliberately unused), so enforcement is by polling (risk_check.yml, every 5 min) rather than exchange-side watching; GitHub Actions free-tier cron is best-effort so the actual gap can exceed 5 minutes, and a fast move can realize a loss/gain past the configured percentage before the next check. An always-on poller would close this gap but is a deliberate scope decision not taken.
